title: Methodology for soil respirometric assays: Step by step and guidelines to measure fluxes of trace gases using microcosms
author: Pitombo, Ramos, et al.

steps.title: Pre‑incubate soil to basal respiration
steps.instruction: Incubate the soil in microcosms until basal respiration is reached (≈1 week under the described conditions). Keep soil moisture at the level intended for the main treatment; e.g., if the treatment will be applied at 70 % of water‑holding capacity (WHC), pre‑incubate at 40 % WHC. Dilute fertilizers or other products in enough water to spread evenly on the soil surface.

steps.title: Prepare microcosm for gas sampling
steps.instruction: Set up the microcosm for sampling by fanning it with a paperboard for 30 seconds, then close the flask and keep the cap‑valve lock in position 3.

substeps.instruction: Fan each microcosm with a paperboard for 30 s.
Close the flask; set the cap‑valve lock to position 3.
Switch both the cap lock and the syringe lock to position 1.

steps.title: Collect gas sample at scheduled times
steps.instruction: Draw the gas sample using the syringe, then restore valve positions and repeat at the required intervals.

substeps.instruction: Perform three pumping movements with the syringe.
On the fourth pumping movement, withdraw 20 mL of gas.
After sampling, set both the syringe valve and the flask‑cap valve to position 2.
Quickly return the cap valve to position 3 (a “deep‑breath” noise indicates proper pressure balance).
Repeat the entire sampling sequence at 30 min, 60 min, and 90 min after microcosm closure.

steps.title: Store and transport gas samples
steps.instruction: Handle the collected gas according to the analysis plan.

substeps.instruction: If analysis is performed in‑house, keep the gas in the syringe and analyse the same day.
If analysis is performed off‑site, transfer the gas into 12 mL airtight Exetainer™ flasks (part number 039W).
Use sample storage for large numbers of samples or when employing autosampler devices.
